clean_tape_measured.method: single-anchor brentq solve on level-keyed-chain-subtracted H3/H1 at 100 Hz L6 (Session 2b Path 2)
clean_tape_measured.note: Stage 8 Saturation Mode menu 'Clean Tape (Measured)' preset. y(t) = tanh(drive · x(t)) / tanh(drive).

chowdhury_attempt_2b.note: Did NOT converge — hit bounds on both a and k. Chowdhury's symmetric hysteresis cannot represent this RE-201's input-stage asymmetry. Retained for reference; do not ship.

asymmetry_finding.note: Smoking gun: at 5 kHz L6 the unit's H2 is 21.5 dB louder than H3. Chowdhury is odd-symmetric by construction (H3-dominant). Asymmetric distortion is genuinely the RE-201 input stage — confirmed by clean level-keyed loopback reference. This is the 'Path 2' branch from deferred_work.md §3.

session2.dominant_distortion_hf: H2 dominant at 5 kHz by ~21 dB (asymmetric, input-stage character)
session2.tape_character: Very clean/linear at LF; mild asymmetric input-stage distortion at HF that dominates above ~1 kHz. tanh Clean Tape captures the LF tape character; HF asymmetry is not modeled in v1.0 (low audible impact at the saturating levels reached in normal play).
session2.chain_reference_status: Level-keyed loopback recorded at 35 (freq, level) combinations — chain gain flat within 0.5 dB L2..L6 across the 50 Hz – 5 kHz band. Verified the chain adds no level-dependent distortion; H2 asymmetry is the unit, not the chain.
session2.stage_8_implication: The 'Clean Tape (Measured)' preset ships with this driveScale. The 'Worn' / 'Chewed' / 'CV Only' presets continue to use Chowdhury with paper-derived params — they do not depend on Session 2/2b.

session3.notes: Farina deconvolution vs loopback, 1/12-oct smoothed, fitted 60-14 kHz. bumpGain near-zero across all heads/speeds — measured response is primarily HF rolloff, no significant head bump. hfCutoff ~9.5-10.2 kHz, little speed dependence.

rt60.stage_5_target_method: T30 mean (L3–L6) — audible-behavior model; sits between T20 (initial radiation) and T60-direct (full modal tail to −60 dB).  L2 excluded from T30/T60-direct means because its EDC dynamic range (~−87 dB) is too close to the T30 fit window upper limit (−35 dB), biasing the slope shallow.
rt60.method: Schroeder backward integration; three RT60 estimates: T20 (−5→−25 dB × 3), T30 (−5→−35 dB × 2), T60-direct (−5→−65 dB linear fit).
rt60.note: L1 (−30 dBFS source) is noise-floor-limited and excluded from the L2–L6 means.  The RE-201 spring exhibits a bi-exponential decay: a steep initial radiation phase (slope ~−17 dB/s) followed by a long modal tail (slope ~−8 dB/s).  T20 and T60-direct therefore disagree by ~2× — choose your target deliberately.

damping.note: Spring is a resonant bandpass (~1 kHz peak), not a low-pass — per-band RT60 is non-monotonic, so an LP-cutoff fit is unreliable.  recommended_lp_cutoff_hz uses the measured passband upper edge as the FDN per-line LP cutoff: cuts HF leakage outside the spring's natural response.

dispersion.method: STFT energy of first 200 ms of IR; 5/95 % cumulative power bounds; chirp duration via dominant-bin ridge descent from 2 kHz → 300 Hz.
dispersion.note: This range is the spring tank's effective passband — i.e. where the spring physically radiates energy — and should set the lower/upper bounds of the dispersion allpass cascade.  Note this is narrower than the Stage 5 placeholder (50–5000 Hz); the RE-201 spring is genuinely bandlimited.

modal_envelope.note: 1/3-octave smoothed FFT magnitude of the 200–1000 ms IR tail (reference level).  Used qualitatively to verify FDN spectral balance against the measured spring.

noise_floor_revvol_max.note: Session 4b — Reverb Volume fully CW (max). Captured 2026-05-14 on the same chain/Repeat Rate/room as Session 4a.

noise_floor_revvol_scaling.note: Only the spring-passband band (500–2 kHz) shifts with Reverb Volume; other bands are chain/room-noise dominated and are independent of the control. Stage 5 noiseFloorGain should treat Reverb Volume as scaling only the spring-passband contribution, not the total noise floor. The +2.5 dB total swing from 30% to max is much smaller than the +8 dB Stage-5 ear-tuned guess — noiseFloorGain at the audible max should likely come down.

session4.analysis_notes: IRs extracted via Wiener deconvolution against the per-level source sweep (chain loopback not used; chain is roughly linear and per-band damping is the dominant question, not chain EQ). Reference level L4 (−6 dBFS source) chosen as the best compromise between noise headroom and spring linearity. See accompanying PNGs for fit diagnostics.
protocol_notes: Reverb Volume position: confirmed 9 o'clock (~30 %) across all Session 4 sub-measurements (verified against the front-panel HEIC photos).  The "70 %" figure in the sub-measurement 1 header of _session_notes.md is a template artifact and should be disregarded.

Follow-up capture queued — see deferred_work.md §4 (Session 4b): noise-floor recording at Reverb Volume fully CW, used to calibrate Stage 5's in-module noiseFloorGain at the max user setting rather than extrapolating from the 30 %-position −65 dBFS reading.

session5.method: Envelope-based fit on bandpassed 1 kHz tone through the RE-201 echo path; single-exp parameters from scipy curve_fit on 20 Hz LPF envelope across spinup/spindown cliffs at slow/med/fast head selector positions.

diagnostics.note: 10-90 closed-form τ is roughly half the curve_fit τ — the underlying motor cliff is sharper than a pure exponential and the data has a slow tail. curve_fit value is the better match to the perceived audible glide; 10-90 reflects the steepest portion of the cliff. Two-exp fits collapsed to the single-pole solution (no slow-tail component statistically warranted). Stage 6 should use the single-pole branch with tauUp_s/tauDown_s.

notes: Recordings: motor spinup and spindown at slow/med/fast head selector positions, 1 kHz live input through echo path, 96 kHz / float mono.

Method note: pitch tracking was inappropriate for these recordings (the live-input setup keeps the playback frequency near 1 kHz throughout; the motor curve is carried by the signal amplitude). Switched to envelope-based fit.
If Session 5 is re-recorded with a pre-recorded 1 kHz tape loop (varispeed playback), pitch tracking becomes viable and 10-90 may give a cleaner motor-only τ.

session6.method: Farina log-sweep deconvolution per recording, dry-through aligned. Crosstalk = peak |IR| at the supposedly-off head's solo-tap offset, relative to the active head's main tap.
notes: 21 recordings (h1, h2, h3, h12, h23, h13, h123 × slow/med/fast). −10 dBFS source level (10 dB hotter than Sessions 1/3) for crosstalk SNR.
Adjacent (h1↔h2, h2↔h3) crosstalk averages −30.6 dB; non-adjacent (h1↔h3) averages −37.1 dB. Slight increase with speed but within ~3 dB band — Stage 7 can treat as scalar weights.

Head spacing on this unit is uniform: h2 ≈ 2×h1, h3 ≈ 3×h1, consistent across all three speeds. This contradicts Stage 1's TAP_FRACTIONS = {0.18, 0.41, 0.74} which encodes non-uniform spacing — flagged for a Stage 1 revisit.

Comb-notch analysis attempted but not load-bearing: Δt = 60–160 ms across speeds places the fundamental notch at 3–8 Hz, well below audibility. The pair sum manifests as rhythmic echo, not a flanger-style notch comb.

session8.method: Repeat Rate knob turned live on the real RE-201 (Mode 1, Intensity 0, continuous 1kHz sine, dry-nulled), Hilbert IF integrated to a delay trajectory then converted to tapeSpeed and fit to the critically-damped 2nd-order step response 1-(1+t/tau)e^(-t/tau). 8 conditions (decel/accel x full/half range x fast/slow knob-turn speed), 1 take each -- see measurements/params/session8_motor_transient.json for full diagnostics.

diagnostics.note: Fast vs. slow physical knob-turn speed didn't change the measured transition duration (all ~45-110ms) -- servo dynamics dominate, not hand speed -- so taus are averaged across fast+slow and full+half. Per-take spread is real (single takes, no repeats); the up/down split direction is consistent across all 4 pairs. Applies to Motor Stop's glide too (shared smoother) by extrapolation -- Session 8 only measured knob turns with the motor running continuously.
